<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. III.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEW.|7}}</noinclude>were ''Magi'', and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Esther 1, 13. 14.''}}* ''Magi'' the greatest about the Prince: or as we read in the Scriptures, of Melchisedec king of Salem, and many other kings that dwelt within a small compasse: or as {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Tob. 2.''}}* Iobes three freendes are called kings. These are commonly called the three kings of Colen, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Amb. 1. Off. c. 12.''}}because their bodies are there, translated thither from the East Countrie: their names are said to haue been Gaspar, Melchior, Baltasar.

''11. Gifts.''] These Sages were three, and their gifts three, and eche one offered euerie of the three, to expresse our faith of the Trinitie. The Gold, to signifie that he was a King: the frankincense, that he was God: the myrrhe, that he was to be buried as man. ''Aug. ser. 1. de Epiph''.

''15. Out of Ægypt.''] This place of the Prophete (and the like in the new Testament) here applied to Christ, wheras in the letter it might seeme otherwise, teacheth vs how to interprete the old Testament, and that the principal sense is of Christ and his Churche.

''16. Murdered.''] By this example we learne how great credite we owe to the Churche in Canonizing Saints, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Canonizing of Saincts.}}and celebrating their holy daies: by whose only warrant, without any word of Scripture, these holy Innocents haue been honoured for Martyrs, and their holy day kept euer since the Apostles time, although they died not voluntarily, nor al perhaps circuncised, and some the children of Pagans. ''Aug. ep. 28. Orig. ho. 3. in diuersos''.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. III.}}}}}}

{{c|''Iohn Baptist by his Eremites life, by his preaching and baptisme, calleth al vnto penanee, to prepare them to Christ. 10. He preacheth to the Pharisees and Sadducees, threatening to them (vnles they truly doe penance) reprobation here and damnation hereafter: and for saluation sendeth them to Christ and his baptisme. Which being far more excellent then Iohns, yet Christ him self among those penitents vouchsafeth to come vnto Iohns baptisme. Where he hath testimonie from heauen also.''}} {{verse|chapter=3|verse=1}}{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=THE SEcond part of this Gospel, Of the Preparatiō that was made to the manifestation of Christ.}}AND in those dayes {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 1, 4. Luc. 3, 3.''}}* cometh Iohn the Baptist preaching in the ‖ desert of Iewrie, {{verse|chapter=3|verse=2}}† & saying, ‖ Doe penance: for the Kingdom of heauen is at hand. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=3}}† For this is he that vvas spoken of by Esay the Prophet, saying, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 40, 3.''}}* ''A voyce of one crying in the desert, prepare ye the way of our Lord, make straight his pathes''. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=4}}† And the sayd Iohn had his garment of camels heare, & a girdle of a skinne about his loynes: and his meate was locustes & vvilde honie.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=5}}† Then vvent forth to him Hierusalem & al Ievvrie, and al the countrey about Iordan: {{verse|chapter=3|verse=6}}† & vvere baptized of him in Iordan, ‖ confessing their sinnes. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=7}}† And seeing many of the Pharisees & Sadducées coming to his baptisme, he sayd to them.

Ye vipers brood, vvho hath shevved you to flee from the vvrath to come? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=8}}† Yeld therfore ‖ fruite vvorthie of penance. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=9}}† And delite not to say vvithin your selues, vve haue Abraham to our father. for I tel you that God is able of these stones to raise vp children to Abraham. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=10}}† For novv the ‖ axe is put to the roote of the trees. Euery tree therefore that doth {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ It is not only damnable, to do ill: but also, not to do good. ''Aug. Ser. 6. de temp.''}}∷ not yeld good fruite, shal be cut dovvne, & cast into the fyre. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=11}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 1, 8. Lu. 3, 16. Io. 1, 26. Act. 11, 16. 19, 4.''}}* I in deede baptize you ‖ in vvater vnto penance. but he that shal come after me, is stronger then I, vvhose shoes I am not vvorthie to beare, he shal baptize you in the Holy Ghost<noinclude>{{rh|||& fire.}}</noinclude>
